subject: pharmacology
title: Targeted Anticancer II: Bevacizumab, Cetuximab, Rituximab, Bortezomib and APL Differentiation Therapy

steps.tx: **Bevacizumab**, antibody against VEGF A, starves tumour angiogenesis across colorectal, lung, ovarian, cervical and brain niches, billing the vascular ledger at class scale: hypertension (treat through, rarely stop), proteinuria (monitor, hold at nephrotic), bleeding (squamous lung and untreated brain metastases fences), arterial thrombosis, gastrointestinal perforation and fistula, and wound dehiscence that schedules surgery weeks away from doses.
steps.say: Bevacizumab bills every vessel in the body for the tumour vessels it starves.

left.title: Vascular ledger
points: Perforation and fistula (bowel primaries at risk)

right.title: Eligibility fences
points: Recent major surgery or non healing wounds

steps.tx: **Bevacizumab**, an antibody against VEGF A, starves tumour angiogenesis in colorectal, lung, ovarian, cervical, and brain cancer niches. Hypertension is usually treated through and rarely forces a stop. Proteinuria is watched, and the drug is held at nephrotic range. Bleeding risk fences off squamous lung cancer and untreated brain metastases. Arterial clots, bowel perforation, fistula, and wound breakdown mean surgery is scheduled weeks away from a dose.
steps.say: Bevacizumab binds VEGF A and starves the growth of tumour blood vessels in several solid cancers. The costs include hypertension, protein in the urine, bleeding, arterial clots, bowel perforation, fistula, and wounds that fail. Squamous lung cancer and untreated brain metastases raise the bleeding concern. Surgery is placed weeks away from a dose.

vis.alt: A diagram shows VEGF driven tumour vessels and an antibody blocking VEGF so the vessel network cannot expand.
vis.caption: Tumour cells release a vessel growth signal, and antibody binds that signal before new capillaries can form. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Cetuximab**, antibody against EGFR's extracellular domain, treats RAS wild type colorectal cancer (left sided benefit strongest) and head and neck cancer with radiation, billing acneiform rash (again tracking benefit), hypomagnesaemia (renal wasting over months), and infusion reactions including anaphylaxis from preformed IgE to galactose alpha 1,3 galactose in tick exposed populations, where panitumumab (fully human) substitutes.
steps.say: Cetuximab needs wild type RAS and a magnesium level; its allergy is a tick bite's legacy.

left.title: Cetuximab territory
points: RAS wild type colorectal (left sided strongest)
Head and neck with radiation or platinum

right.title: Reaction geography
points: Alpha gal IgE in tick exposed regions

steps.tx: **Rituximab**, anti CD20 antibody, empties B cells across lymphomas (R CHOP), rheumatoid arthritis, ANCA vasculitis and pemphigus, billing infusion reactions (cytokine, first dose), hepatitis B reactivation (screening and prophylaxis mandatory from earlier lessons), late neutropenia and hypogammaglobulinaemia with repeated courses, and rare progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy. Biosimilars made it affordable; the screening obligations travelled with the copies.
steps.say: Rituximab empties B cells for a year; hepatitis B screening travels with every biosimilar.

nodes.label: Hepatitis B, immunoglobulins and infection screen
Slow first infusion with reaction readiness
Months: B cell recovery, vaccine timing, late neutropenia

steps.tx: **Bortezomib**, a proteasome inhibitor, drowns myeloma cells in undegraded immunoglobulin protein stress, given subcutaneously weekly to soften its dose limiting painful peripheral neuropathy, with herpes zoster prophylaxis routine and thrombocytopenia cycling predictably. Carfilzomib (irreversible, cardiac ledger) and ixazomib (oral) inherit the mechanism, while daratumumab (anti CD38) joined myeloma's antibody wing.
steps.say: Bortezomib clogs the myeloma cell's protein drain; nerves and zoster write its orders.

steps.tx: **All trans retinoic acid** (ATRA) plus **arsenic trioxide** cured acute promyelocytic leukaemia by differentiation rather than killing: ATRA forces the PML RARA blocked blast to mature, arsenic degrades the fusion protein, together replacing chemotherapy for most risk groups, billing differentiation syndrome (fever, oedema, pulmonary infiltrates, treated by immediate dexamethasone) and arsenic's QT and liver ledgers. Molecular remission by PCR is the endpoint language.
steps.say: APL is cured by maturing blasts, not killing them; differentiation syndrome gets steroids at first fever.

left.title: Differentiation pair
points: ATRA releases the PML RARA maturation block
Chemotherapy free for low intermediate risk

right.title: Differentiation syndrome
points: Dexamethasone immediately, do not await certainty

steps.tx: **All trans retinoic acid**, given with arsenic trioxide, changed acute promyelocytic leukaemia from a killing strategy to a maturation strategy. The retinoid forces the blast blocked by PML RARA to mature, and arsenic degrades that fusion protein. Together they replace chemotherapy for most risk groups. Differentiation syndrome brings fever, oedema, and pulmonary infiltrates, and it is treated at once with dexamethasone. Arsenic adds QT prolongation and liver injury to the record. Molecular remission documented by PCR, not a single glance at the marrow, is the endpoint language.
steps.say: Acute promyelocytic leukaemia is treated by maturing the blasts rather than only destroying them. All trans retinoic acid pushes PML RARA blasts to differentiate, and arsenic trioxide breaks down the fusion protein. Fever, swelling, and lung infiltrates need dexamethasone immediately. Arsenic can prolong the QT interval and injure the liver. PCR defines molecular remission.

vis.alt: Acute promyelocytic blasts are shown maturing step by step into neutrophils.
vis.caption: Abnormal promyelocytes acquire granules and segmented nuclei until they resemble mature neutrophils. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **VEGF kinase inhibitors** (sunitinib, sorafenib, lenvatinib, regorafenib) multiply bevacizumab's ledger orally: hypertension, hand foot syndrome, hypothyroidism (scheduled TSH surveillance), diarrhoea, fatigue and bleeding, in kidney, liver, thyroid and colorectal niches. Their multikinase promiscuity is the adverse event list, and dose interruptions for hand foot and blood pressure are management, not failure.
steps.say: Oral VEGF kinase drugs bill vessels, thyroid and palms together; interruptions are part of the prescription.

left.title: Multikinase ledger
points: Hypertension managed and monitored at home
Bleeding and wound cautions from bevacizumab

right.title: Territory
points: Colorectal later lines: regorafenib, fruquintinib geography

steps.tx: **PARP inhibitors** (olaparib and kin) exploit synthetic lethality from principles: BRCA mutated cells, already homologous recombination deficient, die when PARP's backup repair is blocked, serving ovarian, breast, prostate and pancreatic niches billing marrow (anaemia), nausea and rare MDS, with germline testing as prescription gate and somatic testing widening eligibility. Resistance by reversion mutations restores repair and closes the trap.
steps.say: PARP inhibitors kill only cells that already lost the other repair road; BRCA is the gate.

nodes.label: Tumour cell dies, normal cell survives on BRCA

steps.tx: **Antibody grammar** closes the lesson: chimeric versus humanised versus fully human suffixes (ximab, zumab, mumab from the basiliximab lesson), infusion reaction premedication, immunogenicity with antidrug antibodies, target mediated clearance making doses nonlinear, and infection screening by target biology (B cell, integrin, complement each fencing different microbes). The suffix is a pharmacology summary in four letters.
steps.say: Read the suffix, predict the reaction; the target names the infection fence.

left.title: Suffix grammar
points: o: mouse; xi: chimeric; zu: humanised; u: human
Premedication scaled to first dose risk

right.title: Target fences
points: TNF: tuberculosis screening from earlier lessons
